sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Constructs used for NanoBiT receptor–G-protein interaction assay and cell-based functional studies in pcDNA3.1; surface expression and signalling function assessed. For the SV1 variant (L2/L3), surface expression explicitly confirmed stable across all assays.
sites.rationale: The construct architecture [HA-signal][FLAG][GHRHR residues 1–423] places the FLAG tag between the cleaved signal peptide and the mature receptor N-terminus. In canonical UniProt numbering the native signal peptide spans residues 1–22 (last residue G22) and the mature protein begins at H23; the FLAG therefore sits at junction 22/23, which is 106 residues from TM1 (residue 129) and fully within the large extracellular N-terminal domain. No residue number is stated in the paper, but exactly one extracellular N-terminus exists after signal cleavage, so the position is topology-derived. Python confirmed residue_before=G (pos 22) and residue_after=H (pos 23). Full-length human GHRHR cloned into pcDNA3.1 with an HA signal sequence followed by an N-terminal FLAG tag (DYKDDDD) preceding the mature receptor sequence; constructs used for NanoBiT and functional assays in mammalian cells (PMC7567103). L2/L3 (PMC8501799, DOI:10.1101/2021.08.20.457043) provide indirect corroboration: the same HA-signal + N-terminal FLAG design was applied to SV1, a GHRHR splice variant sharing the N-terminal extracellular domain, with surface expression confirmed stable across all assays.

sources.claim: In addition to clone the constructs into the pBiT vector (Promega) for NanoBiT assay, they all contained an N-terminal Flag tag (DYKDDDD) proceeded by a HA signal sequence, and were cloned into the pcDNA3.1 vector (Invitrogen) for functional studies.

literature_notes: L4 (PMC7567103) describes replacing the native signal peptide with an HA sequence for structural/cryo-EM studies; the HA here functions as the signal peptide itself and is cleaved off, leaving no extracellular tag — this does not qualify as a surface tag site and is excluded entirely. L1 (PMC11423342) reports a C-terminal FLAG on full-length GHRHR; the C-terminus (residue 423) falls within the intracellular C-tail (topology landmarks 380–423) and is therefore not a surface site — recorded in other_positions. L2 and L3 describe the same SV1 construct and are treated as a single indirect corroboration of L5; they do not independently pin a second junction. No ledger line supports any internal extracellular loop (ECL1 186–201, ECL2 267–281, ECL3 348–355) insertion for GHRHR.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal FLAG tag engineered into full-length human GHRHR (pcDNA3, PMC11423342); residue 423 (C) lies within the intracellular C-tail (topology landmarks 380–423), so this tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface.
